candidate.title: Smart-Seq2
candidate.scope: The assigned Smart-Seq2 schematic, from its depicted poly(A)-tailed mRNA substrate through reverse transcription, LNA-containing template switching, cDNA PCR, tagmentation, and the combined gap-repair/enrichment/purification block to a dual-indexed P5/P7 library fragment. This is a single route without depicted alternatives. The separate Smart-Seq schematic on collection page 97 is not the assigned image. SMART denotes the embedded switching mechanism, not another target assay. Library sequencing and downstream analysis are not separately drawn. The readout interpretation is limited to the resulting RNA-derived indexed DNA library; no pooling, genomic-DNA branch, UMI addition, or additional target workflow is inferred.

features: Purple RNA line ends in a depicted AAAAAA tract; this is the biological template for the DNA library.
The card places this RNA in a single-cell workflow; cell lysis is contextual and is not drawn as an operation.
The label mRNA fragment does not show an RNA fragmentation reaction; the primary abstract describes a full-length-cDNA method.

states.label: Indexed P5/P7 cDNA library fragment (caption: Enrichment-ready fragment)
features: Final horizontal insert is flanked by P5 on the left and P7 on the right; Index 2 is drawn toward the left and Index 1 toward the right.
The material carrier for the RNA readout is cDNA-derived library DNA.

The single-cell transcriptome readout samples captured poly(A)+ RNA sequences and their representation through cDNA-derived library inserts. Full-length cDNA supports coverage across transcripts, while each tagmented insert represents only a segment.
The primary protocol abstract states that the method lacks strand specificity and cannot detect poly(A)-negative RNA.
The drawing shows library indices but no UMI or early cell-barcode introduction; it does not establish absolute original RNA molecule counts.

The caption Enrichment-ready fragment is retained literally even though the preceding arrow names enrichment PCR and PCR purification; the graph locates this product after that combined block without adding another enrichment step.
Relative RNA representation can be affected by amplification; the card reports preferential amplification of high-abundance transcripts, so read abundance is not a direct count of starting molecules.

operations.label: Template-switching / cDNA synthesis
operations.description: The G-rich end of the LNA-containing TSO engages the terminal C residues of first-strand cDNA. Template switching continues cDNA synthesis onto the oligonucleotide template, giving a cDNA product with amplification handles at both ends.

operations.information_effect: Adds an oligonucleotide-derived terminal handle to the RNA-derived cDNA, enabling subsequent amplification. The schematic does not establish that all recovered products are perfectly full length.
